title: Asana vs ClickUp
description: Asana vs ClickUp: compare project planning, views, automations, reporting, documentation, permissions, and total cost. This guide does not claim independent product benchmarking or a universal winner; verify current plan details and test both products against the same workflow.

features.name: Core project workflow
features.tool1: Structured tasks, projects, and team coordination
features.tool2: Tasks, projects, and a broader configurable workspace
features.tool1Detail: Start with the workflow your team uses today. Check whether projects, task ownership, dependencies, status updates, and recurring work can be represented without manual workarounds. Official product and plan details: https://asana.com/pricing
features.tool2Detail: Test how tasks, spaces, folders, lists, and project templates fit the team's working model. The breadth of configuration may help some teams but can add setup choices. Verify current capabilities: https://clickup.com/pricing

features.name: Views and planning
features.tool1: Check list, board, calendar, timeline, and Gantt needs against the intended plan
features.tool2: Check list, board, calendar, timeline, and Gantt needs against the intended plan
features.tool1Detail: Do not assume every view is included at every tier. Verify the current plan matrix and test dependencies, date changes, and workload planning with a real project.
features.tool2Detail: View availability and usage limits may depend on the plan. Check ClickUp's current view availability documentation: https://help.clickup.com/hc/en-us/articles/32274881672599-Views-feature-availability-and-limits

features.name: Automation
features.tool1: Verify rule types, execution limits, and plan requirements
features.tool2: Verify rule types, execution limits, and plan requirements
features.tool1Detail: List the triggers and actions you actually need, then confirm any plan limits, usage caps, and restrictions on the official pricing page.
features.tool2Detail: Test the same automation scenarios and check current execution quotas, integrations, and plan restrictions before estimating cost.

features.name: Reporting and dashboards
features.tool1: Evaluate project and portfolio reporting required by the team
features.tool2: Evaluate dashboard cards, reporting limits, and portfolio needs required by the team
features.tool1Detail: Use a real status report and confirm which reporting features are included in the intended plan. Do not infer portfolio capability from a general feature label.
features.tool2Detail: Build the dashboard the team actually needs and confirm card limits, sharing, and portfolio features on the intended plan.

features.name: Goals and portfolio management
features.tool1: Verify goals, portfolio views, and cross-project reporting
features.tool2: Verify goals, portfolio views, and cross-project reporting
features.tool1Detail: Confirm availability and limitations directly with Asana's current plan matrix and test the reporting hierarchy needed by your team.
features.tool2Detail: Confirm availability and limitations directly with ClickUp's current plan matrix and test the reporting hierarchy needed by your team.

features.name: Custom fields and forms
features.tool1: Check custom fields, intake forms, and reporting on those fields
features.tool2: Check custom fields, intake forms, and reporting on those fields
features.tool1Detail: Create a sample intake process and verify field types, conditional logic, permissions, and reporting in the plan being considered.
features.tool2Detail: Create the same intake process and verify field limits, form behavior, permissions, and reporting in the plan being considered.

features.name: Documentation
features.tool1: Check whether project notes and attachments meet the team's needs
features.tool2: Check whether collaborative Docs meet the team's needs
features.tool1Detail: If documentation is central, test page structure, linking, access control, search, and export; a project-management tool may not replace a dedicated knowledge base.
features.tool2Detail: Test collaborative Docs with real permissions and content. Verify export, document limits, and whether your existing knowledge base can be replaced without losing structure.

features.name: Integrations
features.tool1: Verify the exact connectors and actions your workflow requires
features.tool2: Verify the exact connectors and actions your workflow requires
features.tool1Detail: A headline integration count does not guarantee the connector or action you need. Test authentication, sync direction, field mapping, and any automation limits.
features.tool2Detail: A headline integration count does not guarantee the connector or action you need. Test authentication, sync direction, field mapping, and any automation limits.

features.name: Administration and security
features.tool1: Confirm identity, provisioning, audit, retention, and access controls by plan
features.tool2: Confirm identity, provisioning, audit, retention, and access controls by plan
features.tool1Detail: For business-critical use, verify the exact controls, contractual commitments, and plan requirements directly with Asana; do not infer compliance from general marketing language.
features.tool2Detail: For business-critical use, verify the exact controls, contractual commitments, and plan requirements directly with ClickUp; do not infer compliance from general marketing language.

features.name: Migration and portability
features.tool1: Test export/import fidelity, attachments, comments, relationships, and history
features.tool2: Test export/import fidelity, attachments, comments, relationships, and history
features.tool1Detail: Export a representative sample and check what transfers, what must be rebuilt, and whether the export is usable outside the platform.
features.tool2Detail: Export a representative sample and check what transfers, what must be rebuilt, and whether the export is usable outside the platform.

features.name: Total cost of ownership
features.tool1: Calculate current seat pricing plus required features, add-ons, taxes, and admin effort
features.tool2: Calculate current seat pricing plus required features, add-ons, taxes, and admin effort
features.tool1Detail: Prices and packaging can change by country, currency, billing term, and plan. Verify the quote at https://asana.com/pricing on purchase day and calculate cost for the exact seat count.
features.tool2Detail: Prices and packaging can change by country, currency, billing term, and plan. Verify the quote at https://clickup.com/pricing on purchase day and calculate cost for the exact seat count.

verdict: There is no universal winner without knowing the team's workflow and plan requirements. Asana may be a better starting point for teams that prefer a structured project-management approach; ClickUp may suit teams that want a more configurable workspace combining tasks and documentation. These are decision hypotheses, not independently tested conclusions. Run the same pilot in both products, verify every required feature on the exact plan, and compare adoption, administration, export behavior, and total annual cost.

faqs.question: Is Asana or ClickUp cheaper?
faqs.answer: A fair comparison needs the current quote for your country, billing term, seat count, and required features. Prices and packaging can change; check https://asana.com/pricing and https://clickup.com/pricing on the day you plan to buy. Include add-ons, taxes, and administration effort.

faqs.question: Which free plan is better for a small team?
faqs.answer: Do not decide from member limits alone. Test the number of users, storage, views, automation, integrations, guest access, and reporting your team needs, then verify the current limits on each official plan page.

faqs.question: Do both tools support timelines and dependencies?
faqs.answer: Both products provide project-planning capabilities, but the availability and limits of specific views or dependency features can vary by plan. Confirm the current plan documentation and test a real schedule before committing.

faqs.question: Which is better for portfolio reporting?
faqs.answer: That depends on the reporting hierarchy and the plan. Build the same cross-project report in both products and verify that the required goals, portfolio, dashboard, and export features are included.

faqs.question: How should a team choose between them?
faqs.answer: Run the same pilot in each: create a project, assign dependencies, set up a recurring task, automate an intake flow, build a report, invite a guest, and export a sample. Record setup effort, usability, limits, and total cost.

faqs.question: Where can I verify current features and prices?
faqs.answer: Use Asana's official pricing page at https://asana.com/pricing, ClickUp's at https://clickup.com/pricing, and ClickUp's current view availability documentation at https://help.clickup.com/hc/en-us/articles/32274881672599-Views-feature-availability-and-limits. Check details again before purchase.

faqs.question: Did PilotStack independently test both products?
faqs.answer: This entry does not claim an independently conducted hands-on benchmark. It provides a structured comparison checklist and directs readers to official product documentation; readers should run their own representative pilot.
